pages.x: Gaza is a strip of land 40 kilometres long beside the Mediterranean, home to over two million Palestinians, most of them descended from refugees of 1948. Hamas, an Islamist group that does not recognise Israel, took control of it in 2007. Israel and Egypt then closed the strip off with a blockade, and Israel and Hamas fought several short wars.

At dawn on 7 October 2023, a Jewish holiday, thousands of militants led by Hamas broke through the fence around Gaza under cover of rockets, and attacked army posts, villages and a music festival in southern Israel. It was the deadliest day for Jews since the Holocaust. 251 people were taken into Gaza as hostages.
pages.of: killed in Israel, most of them civilians

pages.x: Israel declared war, vowing to destroy Hamas and bring the hostages home. After weeks of heavy bombing, and an order to people in the north to move south, its troops entered Gaza on 27 October. A truce of a week in November freed 105 hostages in exchange for 240 Palestinian prisoners. Then the fighting moved south, to Khan Yunis and later Rafah.

Bombing and fighting damaged or destroyed most of Gaza's buildings and drove nine in ten of its people from their homes. By October 2025 Gaza's Health Ministry, which Hamas runs, had counted over 67,000 dead, many of them women and children. UN agencies treat its figures as reliable; Israel says many of the dead were fighters.
pages.of: killed in Gaza, says its Health Ministry

pages.x: Israel at first cut off food, water and fuel, then let in limited aid, saying Hamas stole it. Aid agencies warned of starvation, and in August 2025 a UN-backed hunger monitor declared famine in Gaza City, which Israel denied. Crowds seeking food near new aid sites came under deadly fire.

The war spread across the region. Hezbollah in Lebanon fired rockets at Israel, and in 2024 Israel killed its leader and sent troops into southern Lebanon. Houthi rebels in Yemen attacked ships in the Red Sea. Iran and Israel struck each other directly, and in June 2025 they fought a twelve-day war, in which American bombers struck Iran's nuclear sites.

South Africa accused Israel of genocide at the International Court of Justice, which in 2024 ordered Israel to prevent acts of genocide and let in aid; Israel called the charge baseless. The International Criminal Court issued arrest warrants for war crimes against Israel's prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, his former defence minister, and a Hamas commander.

A truce in January 2025 returned 33 hostages, eight of them dead, but broke down in March. In October 2025, under a plan put forward by the American president, Donald Trump, a ceasefire took hold. Hamas freed the last 20 living hostages, Israel released about 2,000 Palestinian prisoners and detainees, and Israeli troops pulled back to a line, still holding about half of Gaza.

The war was the deadliest in the long conflict between Israelis and Palestinians. It left Israelis scarred by 7 October and the long ordeal of the hostages, and Gaza in ruins, its people mourning tens of thousands of dead. At the end of 2025 who would rule Gaza, and whether the ceasefire would hold, were still unknown.
